title: M. orygis as an antelope-associated MTBC name
dek: A named leaf that human pulmonary services in South Asia and elsewhere do see. Wikipedia membership is the reminder to keep orygis in the barcode.
story: M. orygis entered Wikipedia as an antelope-associated MTBC later recognised in human TB, including in South Asian series. It is a practical speciation target, not a zoo curiosity.
Pipelines that only emit Mtb versus bovis will mis-file it. The cartridge will often just say MTB detected.
Treat it as TB disease once named. Do not invent an oryx-specific WHO backbone from the encyclopedia.
deepTitle: Why the leaf earned a plate
deep: Orygis is over-represented relative to its Wikipedia fame in some human WGS collections. That is why it is not lumped solely under 'other animal'.
Intrinsic-resistance assumptions should be checked, not copied from bovis by analogy without data.
tb-mtbc remains the method plate; this is the named node for related[].
Wildlife names on the page are etymology. Human-to-human possibility is an epi question, not a lead-sentence ban.

visual.caption: A named animal-adapted leaf that still lands in human WGS queues. The failure is a two-state species caller.

example.takeaway: Orygis is why 'not Mtb' is not a species.
